newsitem.title: ANTIGUA: CRICKET-BRILLIANT LARA CHASES RAIN AWAY.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-BRILLIANT LARA CHASES RAIN AWAY.

text.p: Brian Lara returned to the scene of his greatest cricketing triumph to register his first test century against India in the rain-ruined fourth test at the Recreation Ground on Monday.

With play finally possible after three waterlogged days, Lara contributed 103 of his side's total of 252 for seven on the fourth day, reviving memories of his world record 375 against England on the same ground three years ago.
Until he edged a wide ball from Venkatesh Prasad to wicketkeeper Nayan Mongia, Lara looked in complete control on a good pitch and seemed capable of making his ninth test hundred a big one.
He needed time to get going, taking 25 deliveries to get off the mark, but was in superb touch in the afternoon as West Indies recovered their poise from 82 for four.
Together with Roland Holder, who hit 56, the Trinidadian left-hander helped add 142 for the fifth wicket and reached his hundred in the grand manner by hoisting Anil Kumble for six over long-off.

Eleven other boundaries, most of them through the off-side, decorated Lara's 217-minute innings, but his loss of concentration halted West Indian momentum on a day which initially offered all of them the chance of batting practice when Courtney Walsh won the toss.

West Indies instead lost their first three wickets for 40, including Sherwin Campbell run out for 10 by a brilliant direct hit from Ajay Jadeja, and apart from Lara and Holder only Carl Hooper reached 25.
He hit Sunil Joshi for a huge six out of the ground but was eventually well taken low down by Mohammad Azharuddin at slip, the former Indian captain's ninth catch of the series.
Joshi, who dismissed Ian Bishop in the day's final over, and Kumble shared four wickets and were responsible for well over half the 89.3 overs bowled.
